$comment: Figma↔code mapping for published component sets. The counterpart of design/tokens.json, which does the same job for variables. Component sets are named for how they read on canvas, not mechanically, so this file is what makes non-obvious pairings (Buttons → Button.astro, curiosity → CuriosityRow.astro) safe to rely on. Each component file also opens with a comment naming its set and node id, so the mapping is discoverable from either end.

sets.notes: The matrix is deliberately sparse: Type × Variant × State × Icon yields the twelve combinations above, not every possible cross-product. State is a CSS :hover/:focus-visible treatment rather than a prop. Renders <a> when href is present, <button type="button"> otherwise, and .btn__ghost keeps state changes from reflowing surrounding layout. Primary changes Elevation / sm to Elevation / lg while retaining its text and icon geometry. Secondary hover keeps Body - Small sizing and pickled/500, changing to semibold with wide tracking. Nav hover changes to bold with extra-wide tracking; Inline hover changes to tomato/600 with wide tracking. Icon=ON (`377:2215`) exists on Type=Primary only: 16 / 12 padding around a 28 icon (60 × 52), no label drawn — the component keeps the default slot as the accessible name and hides it visually; hover retains the 28 icon and 60 × 52 frame.

Named ChatBubble because the set draws one bubble, not the thread. Re-read 2026-09-24 after the library cleanup: the sparse User × State matrix contains Talking head/Default (109:1387), Visitor/Default (109:1386), User/hover (109:1385), and Visitor/selected (109:1388). Talking head is neutral-100 with a square top-left corner. Visitor/Default and User/hover share a neutral-white ground, 2px lemon-500 stroke and fully rounded corners, using shadow-sm and shadow-lg respectively; Visitor/selected is lemon-200, square top-right and shadowless. --size-chat-choice (400px) caps the three visitor/user combinations and is unbound in Figma; the set's 879px talking-head width is its library canvas, not a site cap. Interactive Visitor/Default anchors promote to shadow-lg on hover/focus-visible; selected stays shadowless.

Named Avatar because `user` collides with the prop it takes. The Figma user set has no max variant; Avatar adds the three max grounds from the logo set: neutral (`108:1371`, neutral-white/tomato-500), tomato (`108:1370`, tomato-100/tomato-500), and herbs (`108:1369`, herbs-100/herbs-500). Tomato is the code default, preserving the previous rendering. `all` resolves to /avatars/everyone.svg — the asset predates the Figma variant name.

The three separate artworks are not one recolourable SVG: both the circular ground and the base rectangle recolour. Avatar owns the neutral, tomato and herbs max grounds; public/favicon.svg is the neutral variant. Re-read 2026-09-22 for the /resume/cv redesign: the set gained `Variant=monochrome` (`484:2490`, `Type=chat`), exported to public/logo/chat-monochrome.svg and consumed by src/components/Logo.astro, which the 10 Sep 2026 note here claimed was deleted — it exists and is the component this set now maps to, alongside Avatar.astro and public/favicon.svg.

Rebuilt by Max on 10 Sep 2026 as the single source for every mark. The published axes are Icon (17) × Color (5) × State (2); only the combinations listed above are drawn because the colour matrix is intentionally sparse. Hover adds the `md-lemon` effect style without changing a glyph or its colour. The eight footer marks belong to this set and their black/white exports are owned by Icon.astro. Cursor (`109:1373`) is 40×40; Figma Make (`140:1095`) is 56×56; download/share are 28×28; social, AI, mail and phone marks are 16 high. Circle remains a CSS mask consumed by ReleaseNote, square is unused, and every other used entry is ported through Icon.astro. Icon hover/focus uses the shared alpha-following SVG filter: two independent layers with x 0, y 8 and Gaussian sigma 16 each, matching the two Figma md-lemon shadows at blur radius 32. Both layers start from SourceAlpha rather than chaining CSS drop-shadows or shadowing the image box.

Each variant is its own geometry, so PostIt carries four sets of custom properties rather than one shared offset. The paper is 181 × 181 with 40 / 16 / 16 padding, Elevation / md and its own clip; the 500-step disc is 40 × 40 and sits at (104, 0) herbs, (41, 0) tomato, (32, 18.5) lemon, (43, 11) pickled inside boxes of 197 × 211, 192 × 211, 188 × 222 and 200 × 227. Figma rotations herbs +5, tomato −3, lemon +2 and pickled −6 become CSS rotate(-5deg), rotate(3deg), rotate(-2deg) and rotate(6deg) because Figma is counter-clockwise-positive while CSS is clockwise-positive.

Front 114:568 and Back 114:567 use radius/md and Elevation/lg, with no curl. Their 200 × 300 mock is the 200px base width and 2:3 no-teaser fallback, not an image-backed ratio constraint: normal cards use local teaser metadata, or a string image’s loaded natural dimensions, then uniformly enlarge both faces until full back content fits (one-pixel tolerance). A failed 16-step bracket falls back to readable stacked faces and reachable links; successful refitting restores the chosen face. One per-card rAF scheduler covers initial layout, fonts, image completion and resize. The neutral-100 Back uses 16 inline / 12 block padding, H5 and Body - Small; Footer 171:1132 keeps independent Figma/GitHub marks and CTA precedence additionalUrl → githubUrl → figmaUrl. Click/tap/Enter/Space flips with duration/base and easing/standard; hover never flips. Fine-pointer normal-card hover scales only the nonrotating stage to 1.16 while the front is showing; the back has no hover scale, and exit returns to 1, without a focus-within latch. The stage owns one large shadow outside clipped artwork planes; no-JS retains per-face large shadows and both faces in natural flow. State=small retains 87 × 130.5 and radius/sm, now large elevation; its front-only hover/focus magnification remains 2.2989 with adjacent front-state small siblings at 1.5162. Back-state small cards do not scale. The full-face flip buttons inherit the global lemon cursor; there is no component pointer override.

Named CuriosityRow because the set is one row, not the section. It is an Avatar beside a ChatBubble User=Talking head, State=Default and nothing more, so the component composes those two rather than restyling either. Maps to the curiosity collection (thought + question).

The frame's copy (`Let’s be honest`) is final in Max's voice, not placeholder, so it is the prop default. BlankSection is the set's named instance of the general heading-plus-body layout in TextSection.astro. TextSection has no Figma set and therefore no separate sets entry. Body arrives through the default slot because the source is markdown in collection frontmatter. Geometry verified 2026-09-22: the set is one vertical auto-layout with gap 24, and its body is a single Description text layer at y=96 holding both paragraphs — so paragraphs sit on the body line-height with no inter-paragraph gap. The heading binds Typography/H1 with letter-spacing normal, not the tight tracking global.css gives headings; Description is --color-neutral-800.

Renders one position. Mirrors the resume collection in src/content.config.ts. The date range is formatted by src/lib/dates.ts formatRange; the hyphen-minus in "Mar - Oct 2026" is the design's glyph, not an en dash. Re-read 2026-09-22 for the /resume/cv redesign: the set gained a State axis. Corrected State=Default (`114:640`) is Header → captioned collapsed/small ProjectPreview → summary in normal flow with 16 gaps; the speculative three-image media row is gone. Previews wrap with the same 16 gap; uppercase company captions are retained. PDF suppresses all project previews even when passed the same payload. State=PDF (`477:2203`, 1152 × 72) tightens the rail to gap 12 with no top inset, shrinks the logo box to 40 × 26, drops the content gap to 12, turns Header Container horizontal (gap 40, centre-aligned), and drops Description to Typography/Body - Small; Media Container is hidden. Text styles confirmed on the PDF variant, and unchanged from Default: Date is Mono - Small in neutral-600, Role is Body - Bold, Company is Body, Description is Body(-Small in PDF) in neutral-800 — the code already matches; the 2026-09-10 note claiming the reverse role/company weights was stale and is corrected here. The PDF Date node hugs (textAutoResize WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT); its drawn 140 width is the measured width of "Mar - Oct 2026", not a fixed date column. The logo column (`377:1946`) is 40 wide with 8 of top padding in Default. The logo column holds Line 2 (`476:513`) under the 40 slot: a 1px stroke bound to color/neutral/200, filling the column with a 16 gap so each entry carries its own segment of the divider.

Corrected nodes: collapsed/Default 562:5259, exploded/Default 562:5297, collapsed/small 562:5072; exploded/small does not exist. One conditional content wrapper surrounds the text and relative collage in normal flow and grows with real copy: it is a full-frame anchor when href is supplied and a div otherwise. Width/gap/collage-height: 426.759/40/256.804, 665.135/24/408.787, 220.522/8/128.402. All titles are neutral-800 (H4, H3, H5 respectively), captions neutral-600 (Body at Default, uppercase Captions at small). Caption is required: every preview begins with its company, and small reuses the caption styling present in corrected CV 114:640. Exploded text rotates -4deg inside 23.089px envelope padding above and below; layout sizes switch immediately, only transforms use duration/slow and easing/standard. Six ordered supplied assets maximum, with no empty slots or duplicates; zero assets removes the collage and gap. Scraps use top-left translate/rotate/scaleY with reflected slot 5 and remain inside the anchor's hit-tested subtree. Hover, full-frame-link focus-visible and explicit exploded state share the complete presentation. On /projects, rows flow in the normal 1280px container with 144px block padding, 96px desktop inline insets and 64px gaps, alternating right/left. The project-previews inline-size container switches index instances to the existing small geometry at widths <=665.135px, including hover/focus.

Renamed from `tool box` to `Tech&Tools` on 2026-09-22, and gained a Usage axis. Usage=Web (`114:685`) is seven columns of 38×38 tiles with a 24 gap. Usage=PDF (`477:2461`) is eleven columns of 27×27 tiles with a 12 gap. Both render the same twenty ordered entries. Five intentionally unfilled entries display `[tool]`; an entry with an icon uses the exported mark and keeps its name as accessible text. The code file remains ToolBox.astro because the Figma relabel did not create a second component.
The tomato dot is a ::before disc, not a ::marker — ::marker colour is not reliably settable. No content collection exists, so /styleguide passes placeholders.

Renders ONE note, not the feed. Re-read after the redraw on 22 Sep 2026: a rail dot and connecting line were added; a Description line sits under the date; fixed 320 × 180 slides on a solid ground replace the 1px-framed images; the button is drawn in both states; and section labels now inherit the note colour. Inactive colours are transcribed as neutral-600 text/dot/slides, neutral-100 rail line and lemon-100 button rather than chosen. The design's third section label remains `tools`, while the releaseNotes schema field is `tech`.

Renders ONE case-study section, not the whole study, and mirrors caseSection in src/content.config.ts. Re-read from inactive `115:753` and the current active/inactive set `115:755` on 2026-09-23. Both states share one 934-wide main geometry: a two-column header of 489 title + 421 key points with a 24 gap, the 934-wide description 24 below, then the artefact strip after a 64 gap. Active uses neutral-black title ink and neutral-800 for all other copy; inactive uses neutral-600 throughout. Both key-point lists use 12 bullets and 12 gaps; active has a 12 top inset and inactive has none. Both states retain the 16 progress square and 1px rail: active is tomato-300 at -12deg with a pickled-200 line; inactive is tomato-200 at 12deg with a pickled-100 line. Slides stay fixed at 320×180, borderless, and contain their images; their grounds are neutral-800 active and neutral-600 inactive. The frame binds a stray variable `Sizes/L: 24` outside the seven real collections; --space-md supplies the matching authored gap. The frame's prose is lorem ipsum, so /styleguide passes bracketed copy. Scoped scrollbar-width:none and ::-webkit-scrollbar display:none hide strip chrome only; native labelled keyboard/touch/wheel scrolling and the existing 40px/s interaction-latched, reduced-motion-aware drift remain.

Named NavBar in Figma but reads as the site footer: legal link, an "explore with" credit, seven section links and five social marks. Claude, ChatGPT and Perplexity are accessible links configured in src/config/site.ts. Layout as drawn (`114:189`): #impressum and the explore credit at the two ends of the left column; the four section links, then the about links over the social marks, on the right. Icon.astro owns the exported mark paths and dimensions; the current GitHub and LinkedIn assets are 16px wide. Mode is a ground colour per instance, NOT a colour scheme: Mode=Dark paints every mark neutral-white, so public/icons/dark/ holds the same eight artworks with that fill. The bar is full-bleed at every viewport — it has no max-width. The label prop keeps the two /styleguide landmarks unique. Below 48rem the row stacks; Figma's Mobile frame (`103:1103`) is empty, so that decision is undesigned. Icon hover/focus uses the shared alpha-following SVG filter: two independent layers with x 0, y 8 and Gaussian sigma 16 each, matching the two Figma md-lemon shadows at blur radius 32. Both layers start from SourceAlpha rather than chaining CSS drop-shadows or shadowing the image box. Project detail routes render one dark Site navbar immediately after main, outside the detail-reveal conditional.

unbound.$comment: Values the design uses that no Figma variable holds. Each is a literal in code with a comment saying so. Listed here so the next sync can see them without re-reading the file.
items: --size-chat-choice (400px) — the max-width on the three visitor/user Chat combinations.
ChatBubble's 2px stroke (`109:1385`, `109:1386`, `109:1388`) — no --border-width-* token tier exists.
The 48rem breakpoint in NavBar, ToolBox and global.css — CSS custom properties cannot be used in media-query conditions.
focus areas item gap 13px (`114:311`) — no spacing token holds it.

The #ffffff fill on slot placeholders — tool box tile (`114:272`) and CV section Logo (`114:255`). One step off neutral-white and unbound; code paints them neutral-white, invisible against the page ground. The corrected Default CV no longer contains the obsolete three-image placeholder row.
w-[383.108px] on the NavBar impressum column — a magic number, dropped in code.
flipcard state=small at 87×130.5.
Sizes/L: 24 in project sections — a stray variable outside the seven collections, already marked for deletion.
The post-it geometry — the 181 paper, the 40 disc, and the four per-variant boxes and offsets (`114:577`-`114:580`).
The post-it copy's #000000 fill (`114:174`) — the only unbound text fill in the set; code keeps neutral-800 rather than introduce a second near-black.
The share icon's two #000000 strokes beside its #040302 discs (`377:2143`) — exported verbatim.
The .btn--icon 28 / 32 icon box (`377:2215`, `377:2217`) — an icon size, not a spacing step.
The active release-note body fill is raw #000000 (`I476:78;114:335`); Max chose --color-neutral-800 for the shipped component.
The release-note slide box is 320 × 180 (`I476:78;114:349`). Its white 220 × 124 inner rectangle is placeholder art, not a bezel, and is not transcribed.
The release-note date line has a JetBrains Mono Bold override (`I476:78;114:337`) against the Regular Typography/Mono - Small text style.

The page grid — 10 columns, 24 gutter, 96 margin on the 1280 frames; 5/16/24 on the 375 Mobile frames. A layout grid is not a variable, so --grid-frame/--grid-margin/--grid-columns/--grid-gutter/--grid-column live only in src/styles/tokens.css.
The CV section divider line (`476:513`) and ProjectSection progress rail (`115:755`) each use a transcribed 1px stroke; no --border-width-* tier exists.
The triangle mark's 29.686 drawn box (`476:1350`) — rounded to 30 in Icon.astro, as the NavBar marks are.
The /resume/cv header mark size 18px (Figma 477:2404, 477:2385) — a drawn size with no token.
The /resume/cv Education section width, 75.2% of the content column (Figma 477:1955, 866 of 1152) — a ratio, not the 866 pixel value, because A4 is a narrower sheet than the 1280 frame.
The /resume/cv Tech & Tools width, 36.6% of the content column (Figma 477:1961, 422 of 1152) — the same four-of-ten columns /resume gives it, again a ratio.
The CV section State=PDF logo box is 40 × 26 (Figma 477:2203); the code transcribes its 26px block size so the 30 mark centres against the title row.
The /resume/cv @page margin, 16.9mm — the frame's 64px margin (space/xl) converted to the print unit @page requires, since @page cannot read custom properties.
The 1px table, section and swatch rules in ProseLayout, /behind-the-scenes and /styleguide — document geometry with no --border-width-* token tier.
The /playground scattered-card coordinates (986,32; 430,332; 763,406; 1101,482) — page placement read from the Figma canvas, with no layout-position token tier.
CvSection's cumulative triangle turn (16deg per entry) and PostIt's 8deg hover delta — interaction geometry approved in their Figma/component behavior, with no angle token tier.

outstanding.$comment: The Figma MCP server is reachable again. The blocked reads, geometry reads and asset exports are complete; public/favicon.svg differed and Figma's neutral-white ground won. `variableWrites` is now unblocked and is the only Figma mutation still outstanding. `unverifiedChoices` are deliberately deferred code-sync work, not authentication blockers.
variableWrites: Typography collection is missing font/weight/bold = 700, line-height/none = 1 and line-height/relaxed = 1.4. All three already exist in src/styles/tokens.css and design/tokens.json, so the three-file rule is two-thirds done. Each needs a value, a description, scopes, and WEB code syntax (var(--font-weight-bold), var(--line-height-none), var(--line-height-relaxed)) — without the code syntax the MCP emits var(--line-height\/none), which is not valid CSS. The collection has one mode, named Value.

Re-bind the text styles that still hold raw numbers: Typography/H1–H5 → line-height/none; Typography/Body - Small and Typography/Captions → line-height/relaxed. Until then get_variable_defs reports floats instead of names.

Delete size/chat-column (866) and size/chat-bubble (531) from the Size collection. Both are now computed from the page grid in CSS — 8 and 5 columns — so the variables have no code counterpart. size/chat-choice (400) stays: it is not a column span.
unverifiedChoices: Spacing gap still awaiting a Figma read: CuriosityRow's avatar gap.
NavBar mode=default ground = --color-neutral-100. Only the dark ground was transcribed.
NavBar's columns stack below 48rem, and the row itself no longer wraps — the drawn 1280 frame is now full-bleed at every width, so the wrap that stopped #aboutme being clipped is unnecessary.
CvSection's role label drops white-space: nowrap below 48rem, for the reason the NavBar row wrapped: a long role ran off the right edge instead of reflowing.
/resume stacks its note rail under the timeline below 48rem. The Mobile frame (`103:1124`) is unfinished, so where the notes go on a phone is undrawn.
ToolBox drops 7 columns to 2 below 48rem. A second undesigned mobile decision beyond the NavBar one.

ProjectSection's artefact strip auto-scrolls: endless 40 px/s drift, latched off by pointer, wheel, touch, key or focus, temporarily paused on hover. Requested directly; no prototype connection exists in project sections (115:755), so nothing about the timing is Figma-read.
